mode.equityExplain: The money enters the rikma's books and moves the shares
mode.advanceExplain: Recorded as an advance, repaid out of profit splits only — never out of the recipient's pocket
mode.giftExplain: The money moves with no effect on anyone's share

policy.off: This rikma has stipends turned off
policy.collective: Every route, including a rikma-wide programme

terms.marketRate: The mission's market rate is {{count}} per hour. A stipend may not go above it
terms.costShareExplainFull: The recipient alone carries it: their equity drops by the stipend, and nobody else is affected
terms.costShareExplainNone: The whole rikma carries it: the recipient keeps their value and everyone is diluted together
terms.costShareExplainMixed: The cost is split between the recipient and the rest of the rikma
terms.totalCapExplain: This is also the automatic ending: when the budget runs out the pledge closes itself
terms.revenueTriggerExplain: Once monthly income crosses this, the stipend ends and ordinary splits take over
terms.revenueTriggerSet: Ends by itself at monthly income of {{count}}
terms.recoursePersonal: The advance may also be collected from the recipient personally
terms.recourseExplain: By default an advance is repaid only out of splits. Otherwise we have created a personal debt for someone who needed subsistence money — the opposite of the point
terms.scopeBilateral: A two-party agreement: nobody outside the two of you is affected
terms.scopeRikma: Needs the whole rikma: these terms raise the total value, so everyone is diluted

error.rateRequired: A stipend needs an hourly rate
error.rateAboveMarket: The stipend rate is above the mission's market rate — the recipient's own equity would go negative
error.noMarketRate: This mission has no market rate, so there is no share to give up. Propose it as a gift instead
error.policyOff: This rikma has turned subsistence stipends off
error.policyBilateralOnly: These terms dilute every other member, and this rikma allows only stipends that do not. Raise the recipient's share of the cost, or ask the rikma to open a stipend programme
error.outsideEnvelopeMode: These terms use a different mode than the programme allows
error.outsideEnvelopeRate: The rate is above what the programme allows
error.outsideEnvelopeCostShare: The programme does not let the rikma carry this much of the cost
error.outsideEnvelopeMultiplier: The risk premium is above what the programme allows
error.programExhausted: The programme's budget is already spent

propose.titleProgram: A stipend programme for the rikma
propose.introPledge: A subsistence stipend is a monthly payment for approved hours, at a rate well below what the work is worth. The only open question is what that money does to the shares.
propose.introProgram: The programme settles the policy once — rate, a closed budget, and who carries the cost. After it is approved each funder↔recipient pair signs its own terms inside it, with no further rikma vote.
propose.noFunderYetExplain: A programme can be approved with no funder, and the need then published as a request for someone to fund it
propose.why: A word to the other side
propose.scopeNoteBilateral: This goes to the other party only. With no response within the rikma's response time it is approved on its own.
propose.scopeNoteRikma: This goes to every member of the rikma, with what it does to each of their shares shown on the card.

tradeoff.title: What you give up and what you get
tradeoff.without: Without a stipend: {{count}}% of the rikma
tradeoff.with: With the stipend: {{count}}% of the rikma + {{cash}} now
tradeoff.noneGivenUp: On these terms you give up no share at all — the cost is spread across the whole rikma

card.autoApprove: With no response — approved on its own
card.signedByMe: You signed the version on the table. Waiting on the other side.
card.dilutionTitle: What this does to your share
card.dilutionAfter: If the budget is spent: {{count}}% (−{{points}} points)
card.dilutionNone: Your share does not move — these terms dilute nobody but the two parties

counter.title: Propose different terms
counter.intro: There is no "no" here. Propose a different rate, a different budget or a different cost split — and that becomes the version on the table.
counter.clockNote: A counter-proposal restarts the response clock.

pay.body: The cycle closed. This is what {{name}} accrued, from approved hours.

capped.monthlyCap: Capped by the monthly ceiling (the hours came to {{count}})
capped.totalCap: Capped by what is left of the pledge's budget (the hours came to {{count}})
capped.programCap: Capped by what is left of the programme's budget (the hours came to {{count}})

pay.lastCycle: This is the last cycle — the budget ends here

modeNote.equity: The payment moves the shares only once the recipient confirms it arrived
modeNote.advance: An advance: repaid out of profit splits only, with no effect on the shares
modeNote.gift: A gift: no effect on the shares at all

pay.sent: Sent. Waiting for the recipient to confirm.
pay.nothingThisCycle: No approved hours accrued in this cycle

confirm.equityNote: Confirming is what updates the shares. Until then nothing moves — and with no response within the rikma's response time it is confirmed on its own.
confirm.zeroNote: 0 = nothing arrived. The pledge keeps running and it can be sent again — this is not a stop and not a refusal.
confirm.reportedNothing: Recorded as not arrived. The pledge is still running.

toast.programProposed: The programme was proposed to the rikma
toast.countered: Your counter-terms are on the table
toast.matured: Everyone signed — the pledge is live

tab.title: Subsistence stipends
tab.intro: A partner funding a partner: a monthly payment for approved hours, at a rate below the market one. Here you can see who funds whom, what is left of each budget, and how much dilution has actually accrued.
tab.noPrograms: This rikma has no stipend programme yet
tab.perMemberNote: A positive number means their equity grew by funding; a negative one means they traded equity for money now.

funding.title: Find a partner to fund this
funding.intro: The rikma publishes the need as an ordinary resource request. It appears in search, is suggested to people who offer that kind of resource, and whoever takes it joins the rikma as a partner.
funding.name: Request title
funding.namePlaceholder: Funding subsistence stipends for our members
funding.descripPlaceholder: What the rikma does, why the stipends are needed, and what the funder gets
funding.joinNote: Whoever takes this goes through the ordinary joining flow and becomes a partner of the rikma.
funding.publishedWithMatches: Published and suggested to {{count}} matching people

mission.title: A subsistence stipend for this mission
mission.hint: A mission can come with a stipend — a low hourly payment that lets whoever takes it eat while they work on it.
mission.noDilution: The person doing it — nobody is diluted
mission.noDilutionExplain: Money now instead of part of the equity: their share drops by the stipend, and nobody else's percentage moves at all.
mission.dilutes: The whole rikma — everyone is diluted together
mission.dilutesExplain: The work is worth its full value regardless of who needed money, and the stipend counts as the funder's additional contribution. Every member is diluted pro-rata.
mission.voteNoteBilateral: These terms move nobody's percentage but the recipient's, so only they and the funder have to agree.
mission.voteNoteRikma: These terms dilute every member — so the vote on the mission is also the consent to that dilution. The ceiling above is the bound.
mission.onMission: This mission comes with a stipend of {{count}} per hour
mission.seekingFunder: Looking for someone to fund this mission's stipend

fund.coordinateHelp: There is no direct payment rail yet, so this is coordination: the rikma's members are told that someone wants to fund this particular mission, arrange the transfer with you, and record it.

offer.title: This mission comes with a subsistence stipend
offer.investmentSub: at {{count}} per hour — this is what buys the share of the rikma
offer.stipendSub: at {{count}} per approved hour — money to live on while doing it
offer.noteRecipient: The stipend is set against the recipient's own share — nobody else's percentage moves.
offer.noteRikma: The cost is spread across the whole rikma — every member is diluted together, and that was approved in the vote on this mission.
offer.noteGift: The stipend is a gift — it does not affect anyone's percentage.
offer.legal: A subsistence stipend between partners in a rikma — it is not a wage and creates no employer-employee relationship. The recipient is a partner receiving a living grant, not an employee. This is not legal or tax advice.
